Theme

Church life · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

religion noun

belief in God and the worship that goes with it

also a religion, religions, the Christian religion

classical

Cic. N.D. 2.8: religiōne, id est cultū deōrum (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Inv. 2.161 (Lewis & Short)

religiō, religiōnis f.

noun, third declension

religion, reverence for God (the gods), worship

Classically first of all a feeling: awe and reverence before the divine, and so scruple and conscientiousness, a religious obligation or a taboo; then the observances and the whole system of worship, often in the plural, religiōnēs (Lewis & Short). For the Christian faith see faith.

Other words

  • cultus deōrum — the worship of the gods; of God, cultus Deī

    cultus, cultūs m., with a genitive · also used · classical · Cic. N.D. 1.117: religiōnem, quae deōrum cultū piō continētur (Lewis & Short)

    The outward side of religion: worship and its rites.

Examples

  • religiō est, quae superiōris cujusdam nātūrae (quam dīvīnam vocant) cūram caerimōniamque affert

    religion is what brings care for and ceremonies to some higher nature, which men call divineCic. Inv. 2.161 (Lewis & Short)

  • Religiōsior tū quidem es, quam prō aetāte. — Immō nūllam aetātem nōn decet religiō.

    “You are very devout for your age.” — “But there is no age that devotion does not suit.”Erasm. Coll., Pietās puerīlis (not classical)

See also faith, God, church, religious, religious.
